ordered_diagnoses: Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath

facts.raw_span: A 23-year-old man presented with a 1-year history of a gradually enlarging mass on the anterior aspect of his right wrist, along the radial edge
Phalen’s maneuver and Durkan’s test were positive
indicating median nerve compression
Magnetic resonance imaging of the wrist demonstrated a well-defined, encapsulated mass on the radial side of the wrist
exhibited biphasic (central and peripheral) contrast enhancement (target sign)

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a gradually enlarging mass on the wrist, positive Phalen’s and Durkan’s tests, and MRI findings of a well-defined, encapsulated mass with biphasic contrast enhancement are consistent with a ganglion cyst.
The patient's positive Phalen’s and Durkan’s tests indicate median nerve compression, which is consistent with the presentation of a mass on the wrist.
The patient's presentation of a gradually enlarging mass on the wrist could be consistent with a wrist lipoma, although the MRI findings are more suggestive of a ganglion cyst.
The patient's presentation of a mass on the wrist with positive Phalen’s and Durkan’s tests could be consistent with a neurofibroma, although the MRI findings are more suggestive of a ganglion cyst.
